metaTitle: Best Chauffeur Car for a Family of Five With Luggage
metaDescription: Five people and five suitcases do not fit in a sedan. Here is which Emirates Limo van or SUV to book for a family of five with luggage, and when to size up.
excerpt: A family of five with luggage needs a van or an SUV, never a sedan. This guide uses the actual seat and bag counts from the Emirates Limo fleet to show which vehicle fits, when to size up, and what to tell us at booking so the pickup goes smoothly.
quickAnswer: Book a van or an SUV, not a sedan. The Kia Carnival seats five with five bags, so it fits a family of five exactly with no room to spare. The GMC Yukon and Mercedes-Benz V-Class both take six passengers and six bags, which leaves space for a pushchair, a sixth suitcase or a child seat. If in doubt, size up: the price is fixed at booking either way.
content:
A family of five with luggage should book a van or an SUV, and skip the sedans altogether. The Kia Carnival takes five passengers and five bags, so it fits a family of five exactly. The GMC Yukon and the Mercedes-Benz V-Class each take six passengers and six bags, which is the safer choice once you add a pushchair, a sixth suitcase or a child seat.

Which vehicle should you book for a family of five with luggage?

The Kia Carnival if you are exactly five people with five bags or fewer, and the GMC Yukon or Mercedes-Benz V-Class if you have anything more than that. Every Emirates Limo sedan seats three or four, so none of them works for five. The van and SUV figures below are the ones published on the Emirates Limo fleet page, and you pick the vehicle yourself on the booking form before you see the fixed price.

What are the seat and luggage counts at a glance?

Lexus ES300Sedan43No

Kia CarnivalVan55Yes, exact fit
GMC YukonSUV66Yes, with room to spare
Mercedes-Benz V-ClassVan66Yes, with room to spare

Source: Emirates Limo fleet. A luggage count means a standard checked suitcase. Small backpacks and handbags that sit on laps do not count against it.

What should you count before you pick a vehicle?

Get three numbers right and the choice makes itself.

  • Passengers: every person needs a seat, including a baby in a child seat. A child seat does not add a seat, it uses one.
  • Checked bags: count what you will actually carry off the belt, not what you packed. Your airline sets the allowance, and Emirates explains that it depends on your route, fare and class, so a family on two different fares can land with more bags than they expected.
  • Bulky extras: a pushchair, a golf bag, a cot or a large duty-free bag each take the space of a suitcase.
  • Child seats: ask for them at booking. They are available on request, and knowing in advance lets us fit the right vehicle.
  • Your terminal: put the flight number on the booking so the chauffeur is in the right arrivals hall at the right time.

Is the Kia Carnival big enough for five people and five bags?

Yes, and it is the natural pick for a family who travels light. Five seats and five bags means two adults, three children and one suitcase each, with hand luggage on laps or at your feet. The sliding doors also make it the easiest vehicle to load a tired child into at the kerb.

The catch is that there is nothing in reserve. If one of you buys a suitcase for the flight home, or the youngest needs a pushchair and a child seat, you are over the count. In that case book the Yukon or the V-Class from the start rather than hoping it all squeezes in.

When should a family of five book the GMC Yukon or the V-Class instead?

Size up whenever the honest count is more than five bags, or when you want breathing room on a long drive. Both vehicles take six passengers and six bags, so a family of five gets a spare seat and a spare luggage slot, which is exactly where the pushchair goes. On the run from DXB to a Palm or Marina hotel, or the roughly 90 minute drive to Abu Dhabi, that extra space matters more than it sounds.

The Yukon is the pick if you like a high driving position and a big boot, and it copes well with four large suitcases plus smaller bags. The V-Class is the pick for a family who wants the most cabin space, with sliding doors and a flat floor that make loading three children and their bags simple. Either way you are in a private, chauffeur-driven car with the fare fixed at booking, Salik tolls and VAT included, and nothing to pay in the car.

Why not just take a taxi from the airport rank?

You can, but you get whatever is next in line. Dubai Airports says taxis run 24/7 from official ranks at each terminal, and the RTA lists a family taxi as a separate vehicle type you have to specifically ask for. With five people and a trolley of bags, that can mean waiting for a larger car or splitting the family across two.

A pre-booked Dubai airport transfer removes the guesswork. Your chauffeur waits inside arrivals with a name board, the flight is tracked so a delay moves the pickup automatically, and you get 60 minutes of free waiting from the actual landing time. The same chauffeur service covers Abu Dhabi and Sharjah, 24 hours a day.

What goes wrong for families, and how do you avoid it?

Booking on adults only. Parents sometimes count two adults and forget the children need seats too. Enter five passengers, always.

Forgetting the child seat. Ask for it at booking, not at the kerb. It is available on request and it needs to be in the car before the chauffeur leaves for the airport.

Guessing the bag count. A family of five rarely lands with exactly five bags. If you are not sure, book the six-bag vehicle and the question goes away.

Cancelling late. Cancel 24 hours or more before pickup for a full refund. Inside 24 hours there is no refund, so change plans early if a flight moves.

faqs.question: Can a family of five fit in a sedan with Emirates Limo?
faqs.answer: No. The Lexus ES300 seats four and the BMW 7-Series and Mercedes-Benz S-Class seat three, each with three bags. A family of five needs the Kia Carnival, GMC Yukon or Mercedes-Benz V-Class.

faqs.question: Which Emirates Limo vehicle has the most luggage space?
faqs.answer: The GMC Yukon and the Mercedes-Benz V-Class both take six bags and six passengers. The Kia Carnival takes five of each, and every sedan takes three bags.

faqs.question: Does a child in a car seat count as a passenger?
faqs.answer: Yes. A child seat is fitted to one of the vehicle's seats, so a baby or toddler counts as one of the five. Request the seat at booking and it is available on request.

faqs.question: What if my flight lands late and the family is delayed at baggage?
faqs.answer: Nothing to do. The flight is tracked, the pickup moves with it at no extra charge, and you get 60 minutes of free waiting time at the airport counted from the actual landing time.
